newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN chief mocks American critics.
newsitem.headline: UN chief mocks American critics.

text.p: Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali began his annual speech to journalists on Tuesday by mocking his U.S. critics, some of whom claim the United Nations is trying to take over the world.
"It's good to be back from vacation. Frankly I get bored on vacation," he said.
"It's much more fun to be at work here, blocking reforms, flying my black helicopters, imposing global taxes, demoralising my staff and discouraging (chief spokeswoman) Sylvana Foa."
It was one of the few times the secretary-general allowed himself to make fun of his detractors.

U.S. militia groups claim the United Nations is flying black helicopters over America, some Republicans say he wants to impose taxes and the Clinton administration is blocking his re-election for a second term on allegations he has not done enough to reform the world body's bureaucracy.
